climate_pressure: Rising temperatures, heat stress and potentially declining water availability.
documented_impact: Modelled reductions in wheat/crop productivity, labour productivity and household purchasing power.
fcv_mediator: Livelihood insecurity, food prices, poverty and unequal exposure.
possible_consequence: Where social protection, jobs and services are inadequate, these pressures could increase grievances or susceptibility to instability; violence is not an automatic consequence.
uncertainty: Economic and crop estimates are model scenarios, not observed conflict effects.
resilience_factors: climate-smart agriculture and shock-responsive social protection
compact_statement: Heat and water stress can erode agricultural and labour income and raise food costs; instability effects depend on markets, protection systems and governance.

climate_pressure: Drought, declining water availability and salinity interacting with other water-management pressures.
documented_impact: Rural livelihood loss and climate-associated displacement.
fcv_mediator: Rapid rural-urban mobility, inadequate urban services, limited employment, exclusion and harassment.
possible_consequence: Host-community/displaced-community tensions may increase where service capacity and economic opportunities are already weak.
affected_groups: Rural displaced households and urban host communities
alternative_explanations: urban labour-market weakness and pre-existing service deficits
uncertainty: Current displacement figures classify “climatic factors”; they do not isolate anthropogenic climate attribution.
resilience_factors: durable-solutions policy and recognition/support of climate-related mobility
compact_statement: Water-linked rural displacement can transfer stress to urban services and jobs, potentially increasing tensions where local capacity is inadequate. (The United Nations in Iraq)

climate_pressure: Drought and lower/less reliable water availability.
fcv_mediator: Competition among user groups interacting with customary rights, centralized allocation, political affiliation and widespread weapons.
possible_consequence: Water disputes may escalate to violence in particular settings.
geographies: Strongest documented examples in southern governorates
affected_groups: Farmers and other local water users
uncertainty: No basis for a national claim that drought causes communal violence.
resilience_factors: customary dispute-resolution mechanisms and transparent water-sharing institutions
compact_statement: Scarcer water can increase opportunities for violent competition, but escalation depends strongly on governance, allocation systems, weapons and local political relations.

climate_pressure: Water scarcity and heat create greater value and competition around climate-sensitive resources.
documented_impact: Armed actors or affiliates have reportedly bypassed regulations, controlled water-intensive activities or obstructed improvements to public systems in selected localities.
fcv_mediator: Coercion, political influence, regulatory capture and illicit/semi-licit resource markets.
possible_consequence: Adaptation and equitable resource management can become less effective, increasing vulnerability to future climate stress.
affected_groups: pastoral/nomadic communities and users lacking political protection
alternative_explanations: market incentives and broader corruption independent of organized armed actors
uncertainty: Representativeness and prevalence are not established nationally.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and conflict-sensitive resource governance
compact_statement: In some localities, armed-actor political economy can undermine resource regulation and public services, reducing climate-adaptation capacity.

climate_pressure: More constrained and variable water availability increases the salience of allocation decisions.
documented_impact: Local and inter-governorate disputes over centrally allocated water.
fcv_mediator: Perceived inequity, limited participation, unclear responsibility and political mobilization.
possible_consequence: Allocation grievances may fuel protests, inter-community disputes or political confrontation.
geographies: Local disputes nationwide in UNAMI synthesis
alternative_explanations: historical allocation rules and political competition
uncertainty: Climate change is not separable from the broader water-governance system.
compact_statement: Water-governance choices mediate whether physical scarcity translates into cooperation or grievance.

climate_pressure: Water and livelihood stress contributing to displacement.
documented_impact: Climate-displaced populations may fall outside consistent registration and assistance systems.
fcv_mediator: Perceived neglect, unequal assistance, political patronage and exploitation.
possible_consequence: Distrust, protest risk and erosion of social cohesion may increase.
alternative_explanations: poverty and broader politicization of social assistance
uncertainty: Institutional treatment varies geographically; local examples cannot establish a uniform national pattern.
compact_statement: Displacement becomes a larger FCV risk when support systems are unclear, unequal or politically manipulated.

climate_pressure: Heat, drought, floods and water stress increase demands on infrastructure and institutions.
documented_impact: Conflict-damaged or weak infrastructure, limited O&M and fragmented institutional capacity constrain reliable services.
fcv_mediator: Reconstruction burden, weak governance, corruption and prioritization of security.
possible_consequence: Climate shocks may generate larger welfare and livelihood losses because preventive and adaptive systems are weaker.
geographies: conflict-affected and service-deficient areas particularly relevant
alternative_explanations: demographic growth and technical inefficiency independent of armed conflict
uncertainty: Relative contribution of past conflict versus other institutional drivers is rarely quantified.
resilience_factors: institutional coordination and systematic climate integration in reconstruction
compact_statement: FCV legacies can magnify climate vulnerability by weakening infrastructure, regulation and implementation capacity.

climate_pressure: Shared exposure to water scarcity and other climate risks.
documented_impact: Climate and natural-resource issues create common policy problems across communities and institutions.
fcv_mediator: Participation, dialogue, trust and locally accepted conflict-resolution mechanisms.
possible_consequence: Inclusive climate action may reduce escalation risks and strengthen social cohesion, although an effect on violence has not been quantitatively demonstrated.
geographies: Kirkuk example plus proposed national/subnational application
alternative_explanations: Existing social relations and political incentives may be more important than the climate forum/action itself
uncertainty: Evidence demonstrates a plausible entry point, not a measured peace impact.
resilience_factors: transparent allocation and locally legitimate dispute-resolution mechanisms
compact_statement: Climate action can support peace when it expands inclusive participation and legitimate resource-sharing mechanisms.
